title: Mathematics on arXiv — daily notable recent papers, 26 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering by mathematical signals, not measured popularity, and citation evidence is limited for papers only days old.

sections.title: The lower tail of triangle counts in sparse random graphs
sections.abstract: For Erdős–Rényi graphs with n^{-1/2} << p << 1, the authors solve the graphon variational problem for every fixed lower-tail fraction, identifying the minimizing structures and a first-order transition between homogeneous random graphs and balanced two-block models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim every variational minimizer is constant or a balanced two-block graphon, with a first-order transition at eta_*=0.009217...; conditioned graphs are correspondingly close to an Erdős–Rényi graph or a symmetric two-block stochastic block model. (Abstract; Theorems 1.1–1.2.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed eta in (0,1) and sparse edge probability n^{-1/2} << p << 1; the conclusions concern the leading lower-tail rate and conditional structure in this asymptotic regime.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says a different lower-tail mechanism governs smaller p; the conditioned structure is described up to small cut-norm error, not as an exact coupling.

sections.title: Probabilistic ultraviolet renormalization of the two-dimensional Sine-Gordon model
sections.abstract: The authors construct the two-dimensional Sine–Gordon measure by a probabilistic martingale method for every real activity and the full subcritical coupling range beta^2 in [0,4), on bounded convex domains for a broad class of log-correlated Gaussian covariances.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper’s covariance and decomposition assumptions, the authors construct the renormalized measure throughout beta^2 < 4, for every alpha in R. (Abstract; Theorem 2.3.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A bounded convex domain in two dimensions; a log-correlated Gaussian field with covariance K(x,y)=-log|x-y|+O(1), a bounded nonnegative density, and the paper’s white-noise-decomposition assumption; coupling is strictly below beta^2=4.
sections.unique_caveat: The critical endpoint beta^2=4 is not covered; the authors defer construction of correlation functions to future work.

sections.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE₃
sections.abstract: For the Ising model in the Dobrushin square at mesh delta and inverse temperature beta=beta_c-m delta with fixed nonzero m, the author proves uniformly bounded positive and negative moments of the interface likelihood ratio against critical Ising, implying mutual absolute continuity of every subsequential scaling limit with chordal SLE_3.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims uniform-in-mesh bounds on all positive and negative likelihood-ratio moments (and both KL divergences), then deduces mutual absolute continuity of every subsequential limit with SLE_3, with Radon–Nikodym derivatives in every finite L^p. (Abstract; Theorem 1.1.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Square-lattice Ising model with Dobrushin boundary conditions in the Dobrushin square, mesh delta=1/n, and fixed m != 0 in the thermal scaling window beta=beta_c-m delta.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem concerns every subsequential limit and does not identify a unique limit or identify it as a particular massive-SLE law.

sections.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with P_id,w(1)=3 and Irreducible Singular Locus
sections.abstract: For permutations whose Schubert variety has irreducible singular locus and whose Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial evaluates to 3 at 1, the authors give explicit formulas in terms of pattern occurrences and a height statistic, proving the corresponding case of a 2009 Billey–Weed conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: When exactly one of patterns 3412 and 4231 occurs, the authors give P_id,w(q)=1+q^h+q^(h+1); when both occur, they give 1+q+q^h, with h>1. They identify this as proving the irreducible-singular-locus case of the Billey–Weed conjecture. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Permutations w with P_id,w(1)=3, under the hypothesis that the Schubert variety X_w has irreducible singular locus; h is the specified minimum height of a 3412 occurrence, set to 1 if none occurs.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification is restricted to this polynomial value and irreducible singular-locus case; the stated formulas do not cover all Schubert varieties.

sections.title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
sections.abstract: The authors construct boosted loop-erased random-walk scaling limits in the two-dimensional disk and three-dimensional ball and show a planar transition in mutual absolute continuity with classical LERW at boost rate m^2=pi^2/4, alongside macroscopic space-filling behavior at high boost.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that in the disk the mutual-absolute-continuity transition occurs at m^2=pi^2/4; at each finite boost the Hausdorff dimension is unchanged even as unvisited cubes have side length O(m^{-1}). (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Boosted LERW with weight adjusted according to the underlying walk length before loop-erasure; scaling limits are constructed in the unit disk in two dimensions and unit ball in three dimensions.
sections.unique_caveat: The explicit threshold is stated for the disk; the abstract does not assert the same threshold in the three-dimensional ball.

sections.title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
sections.abstract: The authors prove sharp almost-everywhere and exceptional-set bounds for upper and lower intermediate dimensions under orthogonal and radial projection, and construct a measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open sets of directions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension is at most the target dimension, derive sharp exceptional-set estimates from the full source dimension function, and construct the stated open-direction variation example. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compactly supported measures; orthogonal and radial projections; the almost-everywhere preservation statement assumes the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem concerns the specified intermediate-dimension functions and projection settings; its hypotheses should not be read as a universal projection theorem for arbitrary measures or dimension notions.

sections.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
sections.abstract: For stationary Stokes flow through periodic domains perforated by trusses whose width shrinks faster than the period, the authors identify scaling regimes yielding effective Stokes, Brinkman, or Darcy equations and compute effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive Brinkman equations in the critical regime, unchanged Stokes equations in the subcritical regime, and Darcy’s law in a subrange of the supercritical regime, with explicit coefficients for the Darcy and Brinkman limits. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Stationary Stokes equations in periodically perforated domains; truss width a_epsilon tends to zero faster than period size epsilon. The Darcy limit is claimed only for a subrange of supercritical scaling.
sections.unique_caveat: The Darcy result does not cover the entire supercritical range, and the abstract does not claim a universal law for arbitrary perforation geometries.

sections.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
sections.abstract: For each alpha in (7/4,2) and each T>0, the authors claim a self-similar patch solution of the inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic equations whose initially smooth, unbounded-graph boundary develops a corner singularity at time T.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim existence, for every alpha in (7/4,2) and T>0, of a self-similar patch solution with a smooth unbounded-graph boundary for 0<=t<T and a corner at T. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Inviscid gSQG patch equations, with parameter alpha strictly between 7/4 and 2; the construction is for the stated self-similar patch class.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s parameter interval excludes both endpoints and does not claim this construction for the full gSQG family.

sections.title: Foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic
sections.abstract: The authors describe smooth linear and turbulent foliations on abelian surfaces in positive characteristic, give criteria for being p-closed, determine their moduli spaces, and apply the results to construct mildly singular p-closed foliations on Kummer K3 surfaces.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim a description of all smooth foliations of the stated types, criteria for p-closedness, and explicit moduli spaces, then use these results to construct examples on Kummer K3 surfaces in positive characteristic. (Abstract.)
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Foliations on abelian surfaces over fields of positive characteristic; the application concerns Kummer K3 surfaces and foliations with mild singularities.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported classification is for the specified surface and characteristic setting; the abstract does not claim a classification in higher dimensions or characteristic zero.
